guidance:
•Write only in Tâi-lô, the Ministry of Education's romanization (教育部臺灣台語羅馬字拼音方案): Latin letters with tone diacritics, and the syllables of one word joined by hyphens (tiān-náu, sió-khuá). Never write Hàn-jī, and never use Pe̍h-ōe-jī spellings (write ts not ch, oo not o͘, ing not eng, ik not ek).

•A name that becomes code (a function, input, type or keyword) cannot contain a hyphen, because a hyphen is Wordplay's minus sign: join its syllables with no hyphen (tiānnáu, not tiān-náu).

•Use Taiwanese words as listed in the Ministry of Education's dictionary (教育部臺灣台語常用詞辭典), not Mandarin words read aloud in Taiwanese.

•Address the reader as lí, warmly and as people speak, as to a 6th-grader whose family speaks Taiwanese at home. Where Taiwanese has no everyday word for a programming idea, keep the English word (code, button, link) rather than inventing one.

strike.consequence: $~Tse sī tsit-ê tsok-tsiá ê tē-$#count[1|$count] kuá kéng-kò. $banning[Tsit-kuá kéng-kò ē tshú-tiāu in kā tāi-tsì kong-khai ê khuàn-lī.|In iáu thang kā tāi-tsì kong-khai, iáu ū $#remaining[1 kuá kéng-kò|$remaining kuá kéng-kò].]

Lí iáu-sī thang tsò tsuan-àn, iáu-sī thang hun-hióng hōo lí kéng ê lâng. Nā-sī lí kiò-tsò tse sī tshò-ngōo, a̍h-sī í-king hán-kú ah, lí siūnn-beh koh kong-khai hun-hióng, tshiánn siá-sìn kàu hi@wordplay.dev, kā guán kóng lí ê iōng-hōo-miâ kap lí-iû.
